summary: Phases 1-6 of 8 complete and committed. Phase 7 (Deliverables 3+4, cap removal/dedup) is BLOCKED: the dedup-based termination gate was correctly wired (commit 53eeabf2) per the user's explicit strategy (deduplication instead of raising temporalFuel), and it correctly flips 3 rows (K-row, G/F duality row, k=1 of the Gp->F^k p family), but stalls at k=2 due to a pre-existing bug in Branch.lean's ancestorTimes (treats the time-ordering constraint graph as undirected, so a time point includes itself in its own ancestor list once any edge connects it to another time point, making isTemporallyBlocked spuriously true). Confirmed via a throwaway scratch harness (deleted after use): ancestorTimes ord 1 = [0, 1] once a single time-creation edge exists; the k=2 open branch stalls at exactly 2 time points even at fuel=5000 (17x the natural bound of 290), ruling out fuel exhaustion as the cause. Fixing this is out of Phase 7's stated file scope and touches a device the already-landed, already-proven Phase 6 seriality arm depends on, so it is raised as a blocker rather than patched unilaterally, per the plan-compliance escalation protocol. Regression question (outstanding across prior dispatches) is now answered: 0 regressions. All 30 previously-green rows (11 temporal + 19 propositional, the Phase-2-baseline green count) pass with their original expected verdicts, confirmed twice via an isolated split-harness measurement (13 red rows commented out, restored after each run, never committed in mutilated form) -- once against pure Phase-6 state, once again after the Phase 7 dedup-wiring edit landed.

blockers.description: IBranchSaturation's sat_timp field (and truthLemma's pre-existing T-imp sorry) cannot be discharged without a new step-lt-style fuel-sufficiency measure for applyPersistenceFixpoint's own recursion (Scheme.lean, 'sat_timp discharge STOP-gate' comment block, updated in place). Phase 2's branching-rule redesign resolved the determinacy half (Gap 2); the fuel half (Gap 1) is untouched, pre-existing, and scoped as a full-phase-sized undertaking on its own. Carried forward unchanged.

Phase 7's dedup-based cap removal is capped at depth 1 by a pre-existing bug in Branch.lean's ancestorTimes: it collects both directPredecessors and directSuccessors at every recursion step (undirected traversal), so once any time-creation edge exists, a time point ends up in its own ancestor list via the eraseDups'd transitive closure, making isTemporallyBlocked spuriously true for any non-isolated time point. This blocks Gp->F^k p for k>=2 (and presumably every other row needing >1 chained time creation via untlNeg/snceNeg) from flipping. Diagnosed empirically (ancestorTimes ord 1 = [0, 1]; open branch stalls at exactly 2 time points even at fuel=5000, 17x natural bound, ruling out fuel exhaustion). The likely fix -- drop directSuccessors from the traversal, keeping only directPredecessors -- is outside Phase 7's stated file scope (Rules.lean/Saturation.lean/Completeness.lean) and touches a device the already-landed Phase 6 seriality arm depends on, so a fix has blast radius beyond this phase (would require re-verifying every conformance row Phase 6 already flipped). Raised to the user rather than patched unilaterally. The already-landed dedup wiring itself (commit 53eeabf2) is correct and should not be reverted -- the bug is in the device it wires in, not in the wiring.
